notes:
Primary contact: CTO Alina Park. Team: ML infra + platform.
Customer pain: unpredictable token cost and latency spikes during promotions; currently on multi-cloud managed endpoints with high egress + overprovisioning.
They want a dedicated pool with deterministic economics and strong burst handling for traffic surges (promo windows).
Quote from call: "We need guarantees so our sales/promotions don't break the recommender — 200ms p95 is a hard cap."
Preference: open-model variants (Llama-family, LLaMA2 derivatives) with quantized runtime; willing to test Redwood-verified quantized profiles.
Security: require SOC2 + ISO controls, must integrate with internal Okta SAML, KMS keys stored in their AWS account, and audit log exports to their ELK stack.

requirements_summary:
Workload: real-time personalization + reranking + chat fallback.
Target latency: p95 <= 200ms end-to-end for 512-token responses at production concurrency.
Throughput target: sustain 80k tokens/sec baseline, handle bursts up to 160k tokens/sec for up to 10 minutes during promotions.
Concurrency: typical steady concurrency ~250 concurrent user sessions; soft cap wanted at 512 concurrent request contexts.
Cost sensitivity: medium — priority on predictable monthly commitment with transparent unit economics.
Model requirements: 70% accuracy parity with current open model stack; preference for quantized FP16/INT8 models.
Data controls: VPC peering, KMS customer-managed keys, audit log export, retention settings adjustable per route.
throughput_negotiation_notes:
Key negotiation points: 
- Minimum guaranteed throughput (MG-TPS): requested 80k tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool. Redwood proposed tiered MG-TPS with credits — 80k baseline + optional burst credits.
- Concurrency caps: Lighthouse requested a per-customer soft concurrency cap of 512 contexts with queueing behavior; Redwood suggested 256 default with elastic headroom and automatic routing to fallback model for overflow.
- Burst policy: Prospect insists on 2x sustained throughput for 10 minutes / day during promotions. Redwood can offer 2x burst for up to 5 minutes at no extra charge, longer bursts require reserved burst capacity (prepaid), or a pay-as-you-go overage.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask 8 x A100 80GB equivalent. Redwood recommended hybrid: 6 reserved, 2 shared burst nodes (to reduce cost while meeting short spikes).
- SLA & penalties: Lighthouse seeks 99.95% uptime and 95th pct latency SLO (p95) <= 200ms for defined test profile. Negotiation point: penalty currency (service credit vs. % discount) and measurement window.
- Fallback routing: Must maintain authorization & audit when routing to hosted fallback; customer wants signed attestation of no logging retained in fallback path.
- Capacity scaling lead times: customer requests <24h scaling for burst capacity activation; Redwood operations flagged manual infra lead times of 48–72h for reserved GPUs unless pre-provisioned.
- Monitoring and alerts: require token-level cost reporting and per-route latency dashboards; Redwood to add custom dashboard tile for Lighthouse.
Notes: AE pushing for a trial with a clear SLA appendix drafted into the SOW. SE to produce benchmark spreadsheet mapping tokens/sec to instance counts and cost.
poc_plan: Benchmark stage (Jan 20–24): run synthetic traffic to validate sustained 80k tokens/sec on proposed reserved pool; measure p95 latencies at 64/128/256 concurrency levels.
Soak test (72h): continuous steady-state at 80k tokens/sec + scheduled 10 min bursts to 160k tokens/sec to validate burst handling and cache effects.
Shadowing (week 2): route 10% of production traffic through dedicated pool for two business days, compare model outputs and latency tail behavior.
Security & compliance review: deliver SOC2 evidence and run a red-team audit of network flows with customer's security team.
Cost model review: SE to deliver tokens/sec -> GPU mapping + expected burn rates and reserved vs burst cost scenarios.
